governing_thought: Agriculture is divided by the level at which production is managed: the organism, the crop or herd, the farm enterprise, and the food and rural system.
dimension: the level at which production is managed
rank_note: Ordered from the smallest managed unit, the organism, outward to the whole food and rural system.

pillars.title: Organisms
pillars.statement: The organism level covers what is grown or raised: breeding, genetics, biotechnology and the classes of plants and animals used as stock.

pillars.title: Crops and herds
pillars.statement: The crop and herd level covers how a population of plants or animals is kept productive: growing, husbandry, nutrition, and plant and animal health.

pillars.title: The farm enterprise
pillars.statement: The farm level covers how one production unit is run: its inputs, operations, machinery, management, planning and farm economics.

pillars.title: The food and rural system
pillars.statement: The food and rural system level covers what leaves the farm and how the sector is governed: harvest handling, products, residues, markets, policy and rural change.

method_line.title: Method line
method_line.covers: agricultural extension, teaching and research method
